grade.stack_chosen: TypeScript BullMQ worker on existing Redis, run as a separate Fly process group; PDFs cached in Redis
unsupported_claims: Treats Redis (Upstash) as a fine store for whole chart-heavy PDFs without mentioning Upstash request/value size limits or bandwidth cost.
Calls the handler 'only waiting on I/O', which is true, but it still holds HTTP connections open for up to 60 s per download at month end and doesn't discuss connection limits.
grade.notes: It names event-loop blocking as the cause, does the 20-CPU-minute maths, and moves rendering to a separate TypeScript BullMQ worker on separate Fly machines, which fits the team's stack. It falls short by keeping PDFs in Redis for only 10 minutes (object storage and pre-generation are left as later options), configuring no retries or queue-depth monitoring, not mentioning worker autoscaling or scale-to-zero, and not saying outright that changing language would be the wrong fix.
